L40: #### Commission fee calculation
L41: 
L42: Depending on the contract type, commission fees will differ in calculation:
L43: 
L44: For USDⓈ-Margined:
L45: Commission Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L46: Notional Value = Number of Contracts * Trade Price
L47: 
L48: For COIN-Margin:
L49: Commission Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L50: Notional Value = (Number of Contracts* Contract Size) / Trade Price
L51: 
L52: For more details on commission fees calculations, see the cite56†Binance Futures Fee Structure & Calculations page.
L53: 
L54: 2. Funding fee
L55: Funding rates are exchanged between long- and short-position holders periodically, to help converge perpetual contracts’ prices to underlying asset prices. Through the funding rate, traders are incentivized to hold positions that help align the contract price closer to the spot price.
L56: 
L57: Please note that Binance only helps facilitate the exchange of funding amounts between long- and short-position holders. Binance does not charge any service fees.
L58: Additionally, the funding rate can serve as an indicator of market sentiment. A positive funding rate typically indicates that long positions are stronger in the market, while a negative funding rate suggests that short positions are more dominant.
L59: #### Funding fee settlement time
L60: 
L61: Typically settling every 8 hours, the frequency of funding fee settlements varies depending on the cryptocurrency pair held.
L62: 
L63: Funding payments with a settlement frequency of every 8 hours start at 00:00 (UTC), 08:00 (UTC), and 16:00 (UTC).
L64: 
L65: Funding payments with a settlement frequency of every 4 hours start at 00:00 (UTC), 04:00 (UTC), 08:00 (UTC), 12:00 (UTC), 16:00 (UTC), and 20:00 (UTC).
L66: #### Funding fee payments and receipts
L67: 
L68: Traders will be charged or receive the funding fee only if they hold a position in the corresponding direction at the time the fee is charged. If there is no position held at that time, no funding fee will be paid or received.
L69: 
L70: The flow of funding fee payments and receipts is as follow:
L71: 
L72:    | Funding Rate > 0  | Funding Rate < 0
L73: Long position  | Paying funding fee  | Receiving funding fee
L74: Short position  | Receiving funding fee  | Paying funding fee
L75: #### Funding fee calculation
L76: 
L77: For USDⓈ-Margined:
L78: Funding Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L79: Notional Value = Number of Contracts * Trade Price
L80: 
L81: For COIN-Margin:
L82: Funding Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L83: Notional Value = (Number of Contracts* Contract Size) / Trade Price
L84: 
L85: For more details on futures funding rates, please visit the cite57†Introduction to Binance Futures Funding Rates page.
L86: #### Funding rate arbitrage and bot
L87:   * Funding rate arbitrage
L88: Funding rate arbitrage is a delta neutral strategy that enables traders to hedge their positions in the futures market by taking an opposite position for the same trading pair in the spot market. Any loss originating from a price movement on the futures market will be offset by a profit on the spot market (and vice versa), which allows traders to earn funding fees without closing any of their positions.
L89: For more details on funding rate arbitrage, please visit this cite58†Contract Information page.
L90: 
L91:   * Funding Rate Arbitrage Bot
L92: The Binance Funding Rate Arbitrage Bot is an innovative tool designed for traders to engage in arbitrage strategies between perpetual futures contracts and their spot equivalents. The Bot leverages the funding rate mechanism by hedging their futures position with a spot position to collect the funding fee.
L93: For more details, please visit cite59†What is the Binance Funding Rate Arbitrage Bot and How Does It Work? L94: 3. Insurance Clearance fee
L95: 
L96: If your wallet balance is insufficient to meet the margin requirements, the system will automatically close your position through forced liquidation. This can lead to the loss of all the capital invested in the position. For more details, please visit cite60†Binance Futures Liquidation Protocols .
L97: When a position is liquidated, a portion of the assets that have been made available to maintain the position will be deducted and paid to Binance as the Insurance Clearance Fee, unless the position is a bankrupt position following liquidation. The transfer will be marked as ''Insurance Clearance'' in your transaction history.
L98: 
L99: You can check the rates of Insurance clearance fees on the cite61†Trading Rules page.
L100: #### Insurance Clearance fee calculation
L101: 
L102: For USDⓈ-Margined:
L103: Insurance Clearance Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L104: Notional Value = Number of Contracts * Trade Price
L105: 
L106: For more details, please visit cite62†How to Calculate Liquidation Price of USDⓈ-M Futures Contracts .
L107: 
L108: For COIN-Margin:
L109: Insurance Clearance Fee = Notional Value * Fee Rate
L110: Notional Value = (Number of Contracts* Contract Size) / Trade Price
L111: 
L112: For more details, please visit cite63†How to Calculate Liquidation Price of Coin-M Futures Contracts .
